Both edits are clean. The fix is complete and verified.

## Summary

Root cause: `_pad_row` padded the `SEPARATING_LINE` sentinel (`"\001"`) into `[" \001 "]` whenever a format's `padding > 0`, so the later `_is_separating_line` check no longer recognized it and rendered it as a data row. Formats with `padding=0` (simple/plain/rst) and multiline tables (where `pad_row` is a no-op) were unaffected, which is why only some formats exhibited the bug.

Two changes in `tabulate/__init__.py`:

1. **`_pad_row`** (line 2257) — return separating-line rows unchanged so the sentinel survives padding. Fixes all `else`-branch formats (psql, github, etc.) with `padding > 0`.

2. **`_format_table` linebetweenrows branch** (line 2381) — the grid-family formats (grid, simple_grid, …) never checked for separating lines at all and rendered them as data rows. Restructured to emit a horizontal rule (`fmt.linebetweenrows`) for a separating line, suppress the redundant inter-row line directly above it (to avoid two adjacent lines), and consume `rowaligns` via an iterator since it is sized to data rows only (separating lines are reinserted after `rowaligns` is built).

Verification: `python3 -m pytest test/ -q` → **257 passed, 20 skipped** (was 256 passed + 1 failed). Also confirmed separating lines now render as rules across grid, simple_grid, psql, simple, plain, github, and rst, including start/end/middle positions and multiline tables.
